key_insight: Orthogonalized momentum can fail on nonsmooth convex problems when momentum is fixed, but it becomes reliable again with adaptive momentum/vanishing steps and can be strengthened by a new hybrid method, MAGD.
engineering_relevance: For matrix-valued optimization in deep learning and pretraining, the paper gives a practical rule for when Muon-like updates are unsafe and when a momentum-plus-gradient hybrid can improve stability and convergence.
method: Shows a failure case for Muon on convex Lipschitz objectives with fixed \u03b2 and history-based step sizes.
Proves convergence for orthogonalized momentum when \u03b2 adapts toward 1 and step sizes vanish under boundedness/regularity assumptions.
Introduces MAGD, which blends orthogonalized momentum with gradient updates using relative progress weighting.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports synthetic experiments, image classification, and LLM pretraining results, plus theory showing an O(min{m,n} ε^{-2}) convex rate and a matching dimension lower bound.
watch_item: The guarantees rely on bounded iterates and regularity conditions, so the method’s behavior may be sensitive to step-size and momentum schedules in practice.
